label: late copy-phase steps (last ~3 outputs), favoring inputs m/h/i/o/n/r/j/1/u/p
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the <DEL> step, and never at recall_idx 0; recall_idx 1 is almost never active. Concentrated near the end of the copy: 75% of activation mass is on the last two outputs (to_go <= 1), none at to_go >= 6. It depends strongly on the identity of the fed-back input token: m, h, i, o, n are 3-4x enriched, and r, j, 1, u, p are about 2x. Largest activations are L=3 sequences at the final step (recall_idx 2, e.g. q o e <DEL> q [o]); there it fires for nearly any input token, including digits and g. Never fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=0 for all activations), which follows because copy inputs repeat original tokens. The predicate (late copy step AND token from the enriched set) reaches only about 0.49 F1: many late steps with enriched tokens stay silent, and some activations fall on other tokens or earlier steps, so the token and position effects look graded rather than a clean rule.
